instagram_caption:
James Cameron sold The Terminator for one dollar, on one condition. 🎬

He says the idea arrived in 1981, in a fever in a cheap Rome hotel: a chrome skeleton climbing out of a fire. He sketched it on hotel stationery, then wrote the script.

As he tells it, he sold that script to producer Gale Anne Hurd for one dollar, on the condition that he would direct. The budget was about 6.4 million dollars and the shoot was rushed. The Terminator reached cinemas in 1984, and a franchise followed.

Years later he said he wished he had not sold the rights. But the dollar bought him the one thing he wanted: the chair.
